content.text: how to find my anthropic api key

1. Sign in to the Claude Console at **https://console.anthropic.com**. It may redirect you to platform.claude.com.
2. Go to **Settings → API Keys**.
3. Click **Create Key**, give it a name and pick a workspace, then copy the key. It starts with `sk-ant-`.

**You can only see the full key once, when you create it.** If you've lost an existing key, you can't view it again. Create a new one and revoke the old one.

**If you don't see the API Keys page,** your organization may manage keys for you. At Dimagi, ask whoever administers the Anthropic org to add you or give you a key.

**Using the key:** set it as an environment variable, for example in `~/.zshrc`:
```sh
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-..."
```
Don't commit the key to a repository.

**If you just want to use Claude Code,** you may not need an API key. Claude Code can sign in with your Claude account through `/login`.

content.text:
I haven't disabled the workflow. The `gh` command at `/usr/local/bin/gh` is an Intel (x86_64) build, and this Mac is Apple Silicon without Rosetta, so it won't run.

You can disable it either of these ways:

**In the browser (quickest):** open https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/actions/workflows/pr-comment-handler.lock.yml, click the **⋯** menu at the top right, then **Disable workflow**.

**Or fix `gh` and have me run it:**
```sh
! brew install gh        # installs a native arm64 build under /opt/homebrew
! gh auth login          # if needed
```
Then tell me and I'll run `gh workflow disable pr-comment-handler.lock.yml -R dimagi/commcare-android`. You'll also want to remove the old `/usr/local/bin/gh` or put `/opt/homebrew/bin` first in your `PATH`, otherwise the shell keeps finding the Intel one.

Either way, disabling the workflow needs admin or write access to the repo.

input.description: Disable the PR comment handler workflow and confirm its state

content.text:
I fixed `gh`, then used it to disable the PR Comment Handler workflow on `dimagi/commcare-android`. GitHub now lists it as `disabled_manually`.

**The `gh` fix:** I installed a native Apple Silicon build (2.101.0) with the Homebrew in `/opt/homebrew`. That folder comes first in your `PATH`, so `gh` now runs the new version. It uses the login you already had (`shubham1g5`, with `repo` and `workflow` scopes).

**Leftover:** the old Intel `gh` 2.54.0 is still in `/usr/local`. It isn't in the way, but you can delete it with `rm /usr/local/bin/gh && rm -rf /usr/local/Cellar/gh`. The Intel `brew` in `/usr/local` probably can't run on this machine either, so deleting the files is simpler than uninstalling through it.

To turn the workflow back on later, run `gh workflow enable pr-comment-handler.lock.yml -R dimagi/commcare-android`.
